title: Singapore-Style Chilli Crab in Tomato and Egg Sauce
summary: Crab pieces cooked in a glossy sweet-and-sour chilli and tomato sauce, thickened with soft ribbons of egg and served with warm buns for dipping. Messy, generous and made for sharing.
equipment: large wok (36 cm) with lid, or a large casserole (6 litres)
long tongs or a wok spatula

ingredients.item: raw mud or Dungeness crabs (about 1000 g each), cleaned and cut into pieces by the fishmonger, claws cracked
ingredients.note: or 2000 g thawed frozen raw cut crab

ingredients.item: red chillies, finely chopped (seeded for less heat)
cornflour (cornstarch) mixed with 2 tbsp cold water
small soft white bread rolls or Chinese mantou buns (about 30 g each), warmed

steps.title: Prepare the sauce mix
steps.text: Keep the crab chilled until you are ready to cook. In a jug, stir together the tomato purée, ketchup, chilli sauce, sugar and lime juice. Having this ready means the sauce goes in the moment the crab is done, so nothing overcooks while you measure.

steps.title: Fry the aromatics
steps.text: Heat the oil in the wok over medium heat and stir-fry the shallots, garlic, ginger and chillies for 1-2 minutes. They should smell fragrant and turn soft without browning. Gentle heat releases their flavour into the oil, which then carries it through the whole sauce.

steps.title: Cook the crab
steps.text: Add the crab pieces and the 400ml water, turn the heat to medium-high and bring to the boil. Cover and cook for 8-10 minutes, turning the pieces twice, until every shell is bright orange-red. Check the thickest claw: the meat should be opaque white right through and reach at least 63°C.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Stir in the tomato mixture and simmer for 1 minute, tossing the crab to coat. Give the cornflour mixture a stir, pour it in and let it bubble for 1 minute, until glossy and thickened. Cornflour needs to reach a boil to swell and thicken properly.

steps.title: Stir in egg ribbons
steps.text: With the heat turned to low, pour in the beaten eggs in a thin stream while stirring slowly. Keep stirring for 1-2 minutes until no runny egg remains and the sauce is steaming and just bubbling again, at least 71°C. Low heat lets the egg set in soft, silky strands that enrich the sauce rather than scrambling into lumps.

steps.title: Serve at the table
steps.text: Pile the crab and sauce onto a deep platter and scatter with spring onions and coriander. Serve immediately with the warm buns, crab crackers, picks and finger bowls.

tips: A common mistake is adding the eggs over high heat, which turns them into rubbery scrambled clumps; drop the heat to low first and pour slowly.
Ask the fishmonger to clean, cut and crack the crab for you, which saves time and mess at home.
Lay plenty of napkins on the table, as this is a dish best eaten with your hands.
storage: Cool within 2 hours and refrigerate for up to 2 days. Reheat gently in a covered pan, stirring, until piping hot (74°C).
